As others have said, if an individual wants to take their own life, that's most certainly their right as a human being. While doing so, however, I think it's important to consider the impact on their family, friends, and even strangers. I think that a large number of people, deep in depression, fail to realize the impact that they have on people that they may not even know. As an example, I have been going to the same restaurant for quite a few years; if I was to suddenly die, I strongly suspect that the manager, whom I have frequently engaged in small-talk, would be a bit upset to hear about it. My point is that when a person passes away, cumulatively, they have a pretty big impact, and on people they might not even know very well.

I am by no means the most intelligent individual in the world, but it's fairly easy for me to see that if I was to kill myself, a LOT of people would be negatively impacted by it, and I don't even have that many close friends.
